hook: *LeBron* or *Jordan*? At 41, one of them is still making his case.
dek: LeBron is in his 24th season, now with the Sixers. Curry and KD are 38. A Warriors rookie is scoring 21. The Den makes the call.

slides.label: The case for Jordan
slides.text: *6 rings, 6 Finals MVPs*, never lost in the Finals. *5 MVPs, 10 scoring titles.* The highest peak the game has ever seen.

slides.label: The case for LeBron
slides.text: *All-time leading scorer.* *4 rings with 3 franchises*, 4 Finals MVPs, 4 MVPs and *10 Finals trips*.

slides.label: Still going
slides.text: Now *41*, in his *24th season*, the most in NBA history. He signed with the *Sixers* this summer and hit the go-ahead bucket on the Knicks Oct. 30.

slides.label: The Den's pick
slides.text: *LeBron*, because of *longevity*. Great for longer than some players have been alive. When he leaves, *the game won't be the same*.

slides.label: Curry and KD
slides.text: Both *38*, both still cooking: Curry *29.9 a game*, KD *20.8* in Houston. They are the *last chapter* of this generation, not the next one.

slides.label: The wild card
slides.text: *Yaxel Lendeborg*: No. 11 pick, Warriors rookie, *21 a game* through nine. Only *11 high school games*. Parents hooped in *Puerto Rico and the DR*.

slides.label: From the warehouse
slides.text: Warehouse job, then *junior college in Arizona*, UAB, a *national title at Michigan*. Kerr: *"He's one of our best players already."*

cta_line: Jordan set the bar. *LeBron stretched it.*
question: Who's your GOAT: LeBron or Jordan?

LeBron or Jordan? The argument every barbershop has had just got a new chapter.

Jordan went 6 for 6 in the Finals with 6 Finals MVPs, 5 MVPs and 10 scoring titles. LeBron is the all-time leading scorer with 4 rings across 3 franchises and 10 Finals trips, and at 41 he is playing his 24th season, the most in NBA history, now with the Sixers.

caption_linkedin:
The LeBron vs. Jordan debate is really a debate about two kinds of excellence: peak and longevity.

Jordan's case is the peak: 6 championships, 6 Finals MVPs and a perfect Finals record. LeBron's case is the long game: the all-time scoring record, 4 championships with 3 franchises, 10 Finals appearances and, at 41, a 24th season, the most in NBA history, with a new team.

Our call is LeBron. Sustaining elite performance across two decades, through new teams, new systems and every new generation coming for your spot, may be the harder thing to do.

The same question applies in business. Do you build for the perfect run, or for the career?

By The Innovators Den.
